quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'It'. 'In November' uses 'in' with months.
quests.explanation: Subject (It) + rains (verb) + heavily (manner) + in November (time). Months always use 'in': in January, in August, in November.
quests.textToSpeak: It rains heavily in November.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. The adjective 'warm' comes before the noun.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + wears (verb) + a warm coat (object) + today (time). Adjectives like 'warm' appear directly before the noun they describe.
quests.textToSpeak: She wears a warm coat today.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The snow'. 'On the mountains' uses 'on' for surfaces.
quests.explanation: Subject (The snow) + falls (verb) + on the mountains (place). 'On' is used when something rests on or covers a surface.
quests.textToSpeak: The snow falls on the mountains.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The bird'. 'In the morning' uses 'in' with parts of the day.
quests.explanation: Subject (The bird) + sings (verb) + in the morning (time). Time-of-day phrases - in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening - all use 'in'.
quests.textToSpeak: The bird sings in the morning.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Her cat' receives the food. 'Dry food' is what she gives.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + feeds (verb) + her cat (indirect object) + dry food (direct object). 'Feed' takes two objects: the animal and the food.
quests.textToSpeak: She feeds her cat dry food.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The fish'. 'In the pond' tells us where.
quests.explanation: Subject (The fish) + swim (verb) + in the pond (place). 'Fish' is both singular and plural - one fish, two fish.
quests.textToSpeak: The fish swim in the pond.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. The color comes before the noun. 'Today' comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + wears (verb) + a blue dress (object) + today (time). Color adjectives always come before the noun in English.
quests.textToSpeak: She wears a blue dress today.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The red car'. 'Very' intensifies 'fast'.
quests.explanation: Subject (The red car) + drives (verb) + very fast (manner). 'Very' is an intensifier strengthening the adverb 'fast'.
quests.textToSpeak: The red car drives very fast.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. Two words describe the resulting color.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + paints (verb) + the wall (object) + bright white (result). 'Paint something a color' describes the color the surface becomes.
quests.textToSpeak: He paints the wall bright white.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'Class'. Two time phrases combine: 'at eight' and 'in the morning'.
quests.explanation: Subject (Class) + starts (verb) + at eight in the morning (time). 'At' is used for specific times; 'in the morning' specifies the part of day.
quests.textToSpeak: Class starts at eight in the morning.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Wakes up' is a phrasal verb. 'At six thirty' is the time.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + wakes up (phrasal verb) + at six thirty (time). 'Wake up' is a common phrasal verb meaning to stop sleeping.
quests.textToSpeak: She wakes up at six thirty.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The store'. 'At nine' is the time. 'Tonight' comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (The store) + closes (verb) + at nine tonight (time). 'At' precedes clock times; 'tonight' specifies this particular evening.
quests.textToSpeak: The store closes at nine tonight.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Please' begins a polite request. The manner adverb comes last.
quests.explanation: 'Please' makes this a polite imperative: open (verb) + the window (object) + carefully (manner). 'Please' at the start softens a command into a polite request.
quests.textToSpeak: Please open the window carefully.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Turns off' is a phrasal verb. 'At bedtime' ends it.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + turns off (phrasal verb) + the lights (object) + at bedtime (time). 'Turn off' is a separable phrasal verb; the object can go between 'turn' and 'off'.
quests.textToSpeak: She turns off the lights at bedtime.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'Every night' is a frequency time phrase at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + locks (verb) + the door (object) + every night (frequency). 'Every night' shows this is a repeated, habitual action.
quests.textToSpeak: He locks the door every night.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The students'. 'Take notes' is a fixed collocation.
quests.explanation: Subject (The students) + take notes (verb phrase) + in class (place). 'Take notes' is a fixed expression meaning to write down information while listening.
quests.textToSpeak: The students take notes in class.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'To answer' explains why she raises her hand.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + raises (verb) + her hand (object) + to answer (purpose). 'To + verb' expresses purpose - she raises her hand in order to answer.
quests.textToSpeak: She raises her hand to answer.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'On time' means at the correct moment - not late.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + submits (verb) + his homework (object) + on time (manner). 'On time' means not late; contrast with 'in time' which means early enough.
quests.textToSpeak: He submits his homework on time.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'To work' is the destination.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + takes the bus (verb + transport) + to work (destination). 'Take the bus/train/tram' is the standard English phrase for using public transport.
quests.textToSpeak: She takes the bus to work.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'To school' is the destination.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + rides (verb) + his bike (object) + to school (destination). 'Ride' is used with bikes, horses, and motorbikes - vehicles you sit on top of.
quests.textToSpeak: He rides his bike to school.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'They'. 'To the airport' is the destination. 'Early' comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + drive (verb) + to the airport (destination) + early (time). 'Early' here suggests they leave before the usual expected time.
quests.textToSpeak: They drive to the airport early.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Very' intensifies 'happy'. 'Today' comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + feels (linking verb) + very happy (adjective) + today (time). 'Feel' is a linking verb followed by an adjective - never an adverb.
quests.textToSpeak: She feels very happy today.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'After work' is a time expression at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + is (linking verb) + tired (adjective) + after work (time). 'After work' is a common phrase meaning following the end of the working day.
quests.textToSpeak: He is tired after work.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'They'. 'Excited about' is a fixed adjective + preposition.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + are (linking verb) + excited (adjective) + about the trip (phrase). 'Excited about' is a collocation - 'about' is always used with 'excited'.
quests.textToSpeak: They are excited about the trip.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Playing soccer' is a participial phrase telling us when.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + hurt (past verb) + her knee (object) + playing soccer (context). The -ing phrase tells us during what activity the injury happened.
quests.textToSpeak: She hurt her knee playing soccer.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'Every morning' is a time expression at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + stretches (verb) + his arms (object) + every morning (frequency). 'Every morning' describes a repeated daily habit.
quests.textToSpeak: He stretches his arms every morning.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The nurse'. 'Patient's' uses an apostrophe for possession.
quests.explanation: Subject (The nurse) + checks (verb) + the patient's temperature (object). 'Patient's' uses apostrophe + s to show possession - the temperature belongs to the patient.
quests.textToSpeak: The nurse checks the patient's temperature.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'To visit Paris' is an infinitive of intention. 'Soon' comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + plans (verb) + to visit Paris (infinitive phrase) + soon (time). 'Plan + to + verb' expresses a future intention.
quests.textToSpeak: She plans to visit Paris soon.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. Two infinitives appear: 'to learn' and 'to cook'.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + wants (verb) + to learn (infinitive 1) + to cook (infinitive 2). Two infinitives can follow each other: 'want to learn to do something'.
quests.textToSpeak: He wants to learn to cook.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'They'. 'Going to the cinema' is a future plan. 'Tomorrow' ends it.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + are going (present continuous) + to the cinema (destination) + tomorrow (time). Present continuous with a future time word expresses a planned future event.
quests.textToSpeak: They are going to the cinema tomorrow.
